exercices.instructions_en: Vasco custom face pull variation using doorframe or towel for rear delt development. Zero equipment. Part of Tuesday Pull day.
Vasco custom single-arm hammer curl for 5kg dumbbell. Targets brachialis for arm thickness. Part of Tuesday Pull day.

Vasco custom dead bug - foundational deep core stability and anti-extension. Teaches lumbar-pelvic dissociation, breath-coordination, and proximal stability for distal mobility. Prerequisite for all core training.
Vasco custom forearm plank - foundational anterior core stability exercise. Teaches full-body tension, breath control, and anti-extension. Prerequisite for all advanced core work.
Vasco custom bird dog - foundational contralateral limb coordination and lumbar stability. Teaches hip dissociation from spine, glute activation, and scapular control.
Vasco custom side plank - foundational lateral core stability. Targets obliques, QL, and hip abductors. Essential for spinal stability and rotational control.
Vasco custom hollow body hold - foundational anti-extension core stability. Teaches global anterior chain tension, breath control under load, and positional awareness for gymnastics/calisthenics.

Secure Band above you.

  1. Stand facing band, with feet hip-width apart.
  2. Bend your knees slightly to engage your core.
  3. Keep your chest up, pin your shoulder blades back, and tuck your elbows tightly to the sides of your torso.
  4. Exhale and pull the band straight down toward your thighs.
  5. Inhale and slowly control the band as you let your arms return upwards to their starting position.

1. Stand facing a wall. Place your forearms vertically against the wall so your elbows and wrists are both touching it.
  2. Point your arms slightly outwards from "straight up".
  3. Protract your shoulders had, then slide your forearms up the wall until your elbows are about level with your chin.
  4. Slide your forearms back down the wall. Repeat as necessary.

1. Hold the barbell on your shoulders as if to squat.
  2. Take a half-step forwards with one leg, placing your foot on the ground.
  3. Lock the front leg, and either lock your back leg or allow it to bend very slightly.
  4. Bend forwards under control to stretch the rear of your front leg, then return to your standing position.

Repeat as necessary for reps/time. You should also repeat for the other leg.

1. Stand facing away from a bench, couch or similar-height object.
  2. Extend one leg backwards, resting your foot "laces-down" on the edge of the bench.
  3. Lower yourself until your rear knee is on the floor and you are in a lunge position, with your torso hanging forwards slightly.
  4. Brace your core, tense your rear glute, and straighten up your torso to vertical, under control. Relax and repeat.

Repeat for the other leg, too.

1. Hold the resistance band (or any other rope-like object, the elasticity is not necessary) above your head, between your hands, with your arms straight. Pull it taught to engage your lats.
  2. Step forwards into a lunge, dropping until your knee is almost touching the floor.
  3. Slowly and controlledly pulse your body up and down by about an inch. Repeat for required reps.
  4. Repeat for other leg.

1. Start kneeling.
  2. Extend one leg out forwards, fully straightened. Follow with your hips so your back leg begins to unfold.
  3. Carefully lower yourself into the stretch. Do not go beyond your limit.
  4. Hold for the required time.

exercices.nom_fr: Étirement squat bras vers le ciel
exercices.instructions_en:
1. Drop into a squat.
  2. Hold one ankle with the opposite hand.
  3. Fold your other arm to your chest.
  4. Staying in the squat and keeping hold of your ankle, twist to turn your chest-hand back/outwards until your elbow is pointing at the sky.
  5. Return to the neutral squatting position with your hand on your chest. Repeat movement as required.

Repeat on both sides.

Explosive Push-Ups

Start in a standard push-up position, lower your chest, then explosively push off the ground so your hands leave the floor. Land softly and immediately repeat.

Russian Push-Ups

Start in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Lower your chest toward the floor, then shift your body forward while keeping your chest close to the ground. Extend your arms to return to the starting position, then reverse the movement smoothly. Keep your core tight and maintain controlled movement throughout the exercise.

A straight-arm calisthenics static hold where you assume a plank position and lean the shoulders as far forward as possible past the wrists with protracted scapulae and a hollow body.

Lie on you back with your hips and knees flexed, feet on the ground. From this position, raise your butt off of the ground to a height where your body makes a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. To make the exercise more intense, you can add weight by letting a barbell rest on your hips as you complete the motion, or you can put your feet on a slightly higher surface such as a step or a bench.
An isometric leg extension is a strengthening exercise where you contract your quadriceps muscles against an immovable resistance without changing the length of the muscle or moving your knee joint.
A bench press isometric hold is a static strength exercise where you pause and hold a barbell or dumbbells either at your chest, mid-press, or at lockout without moving for a set time
An isometric overhead press involves holding a weight statically overhead or pushing against an immovable object at a specific point in the press without moving the joint.
An isometric lateral raise is a shoulder exercise where you hold your arms out to the sides at waist height for a set amount of time instead of moving up and down
An isometric preacher curl is a static strength exercise where you hold a fixed position on a preacher pad or and inclined bench under tension without moving the joint.

An isometric Lat pulldown is a strength-building exercise where you pull the bar down to your chest and hold the contracted position at the bottom without moving your limbs for a set number of seconds

A single-arm isometric or isolated triceps pushdown is an isolation cable exercise where you pin your upper arm against your torso, hinge at the hips, and extend the elbow to achieve a peak contraction in the triceps muscle.

Wrist circles is warm-up exercise, where you rotate your wrists in a circular motion. They improve mobility and are recommended before exercises such as pull ups, hand stands and other exercises that put pressure on your wrists.
